mainTopic: End of פרק השוחט; the משנה listing the טרפות; and the Torah sources for whether a טרפה can live
overview: The amud opens by finishing the last discussion of פרק השוחט. The גמרא explains that רבי אלעזר's ruling was needed because a wife may have miscarried privately, which still obligates her in a קרבן יולדת. A הדרן then closes the chapter. A new משנה opens פרק אלו טרפות and lists injuries that make an animal a טרפה, forbidden even after proper שחיטה. The list includes the וושט, גרגרת, brain membrane, heart, spine, liver, lung, stomachs, intestines, a fall, broken ribs, and a predator's clawing. It ends with the rule that any animal that could not survive in such a condition is a טרפה. In the גמרא, ריש לקיש looks for a Torah hint that a טרפה cannot live, and finds it in "וזאת החיה אשר תאכלו". The גמרא then searches for the source of the opposing view that a טרפה can live. It ends with a ברייתא about eighteen טרפות told to משה at סיני, and then challenges that number, since more cases seem to exist.

steps.title: Why the ruling was needed: she may have miscarried
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that we might have thought the slaughter is fine because a real birth would be public knowledge. רבי אלעזר teaches that it is still a problem, because she may have miscarried privately.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: if she really had given birth, people would know about it. So we would think the slaughter is fine, since she obviously did not give birth. That is why he teaches us that it is not fine: say that she miscarried, which people would not necessarily know about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why רבי אלעזר needed to state his ruling at all. It shows that there was a reasonable mistake someone could have made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken thought was that a birth always becomes public, so a claim of a birth-offering with no known birth means nothing. The answer is that a miscarriage can happen quietly and still obligate a קרבן יולדת. So the stated intention could be real, and the slaughter is affected.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said: it introduces a mistaken assumption the teaching comes to rule out
A voice, meaning publicity or common knowledge
He teaches us, meaning this is the new point of the ruling
She miscarried

steps.whatToRemember: A miscarriage also obligates a woman in a קרבן יולדת, so 'nobody heard about a birth' does not prove there is no obligation.

phrases.english: You might have said:
If it were so that she gave birth,
phrases.notes: 'She' is the slaughterer's wife, from the case discussed just before this.

phrases.english: there would have been publicity about it,
so he teaches us:
Say that she miscarried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from before this section about why רבי אלעזר's ruling needed to be stated.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: it identifies a reasonable mistake the ruling comes to prevent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A birth would be public, so with no known birth the stated intention is empty and the slaughter is valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: She may have miscarried without anyone knowing, so the intention could be real and the slaughter is not valid.

steps.title: Hadran: closing the chapter of השוחט
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marking the end of פרק השוחט.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter השוחט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא formally closes the second chapter of חולין, פרק השוחט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is not an argument. It is the traditional way of finishing a chapter, expressing the hope to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the formula said when finishing a chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, HaShochet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter whose last discussion ended in the previous step.

steps.title: The משנה begins listing טרפות
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter opens by listing injuries that make an animal a טרפה: a pierced gullet, a cut windpipe, a pierced brain membrane, a heart pierced into its chamber, a broken spine with a severed cord, and a liver that is completely gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: These make an animal a טרפה: a gullet with a hole in it, a windpipe that was cut, a hole in the brain's membrane, a hole in the heart that reaches its inner chamber, a broken spine whose cord is cut, and a liver that was removed with nothing left of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The new משנה starts a list of injuries that make an animal forbidden to eat even if it was slaughtered properly. This first part covers six injuries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item states exactly how serious the injury must be. The heart must be pierced into its chamber, the spine must be broken with the cord cut too, and the liver must be completely gone. A smaller version of these injuries is not on this list.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal injury or defect, forbidden to eat even after proper שחיטה
The gullet (esophagus), the food pipe
The windpipe (trachea)
The membrane covering the brain
The spinal cord

steps.confusionAlert: For the וושט, any hole through it is enough. For the גרגרת, the משנה says 'cut' (פסוקה), not just pierced. The words are different on purpose.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list is the base for the whole chapter of טרפות, which is central to the practical laws of כשרות.

phrases.english: MISHNA: These are tereifot in an animal:
a perforated gullet, and a cut windpipe;
if the membrane of the brain was perforated;
if the heart was perforated into its chamber;
if the spine was broken and its cord was cut;

phrases.aramaic: נִיטַּל הַכָּבֵד וְלֹא נִשְׁתַּיֵּיר הֵימֶנּוּ כְּלוּם.
phrases.english: if the liver was removed and nothing at all remained of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pierced וושט, a cut גרגרת, a pierced brain membrane, a heart pierced into its chamber, a broken spine with a severed cord, and a completely missing liver each make an animal a טרפה.

steps.title: A pierced or damaged lung, and רבי שמעון's view
steps.stepSummary: A lung with a hole or a missing piece makes the animal a טרפה. רבי שמעון says the hole must reach the bronchial tubes.
steps.simpleTranslation: A lung with a hole in it, or with a piece missing, makes the animal a טרפה. רבי שמעון says it is only a טרפה if the hole goes through into the airways.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds the lung to the list and records a disagreement about how deep the hole must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion (תנא קמא) treats any hole in the lung as a טרפה. רבי שמעון says a hole that does not reach the סמפונות, the inner air tubes, is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The lung
Was missing a piece
The bronchial tubes, the air passages inside the lung
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה

phrases.english: A lung that was perforated or that was missing a piece;
Rabbi Shimon says:
Not unless it is perforated through to the bronchi.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, a pierced or deficient lung is a טרפה. רבי שמעון says it is only a טרפה if the hole reaches the סמפונות.

steps.title: Stomach, gallbladder, intestines, and the rumen
steps.stepSummary: A hole in the קבה, the gallbladder, or the small intestines makes the animal a טרפה. The inner rumen becomes a טרפה with any hole, and the outer rumen only with a tear across most of it. רבי יהודה gives different measurements for large and small animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the abomasum, the gallbladder, or the small intestines got a hole, the animal is a טרפה. The inner part of the rumen is a טרפה with any hole, and the outer part only if most of it is torn. רבי יהודה says: in a large animal a tear of a טפח is enough, and in a small animal it must be most of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the list with digestive organs and records רבי יהודה's view on how big a tear in the outer rumen must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner and outer parts of the כרס are treated differently: any hole in the inner part, but most of the outer part must be torn. רבי יהודה changes the measure for large animals to a fixed טפח, while for small animals he keeps 'most of it.'

keyTerms.meaning: The abomasum, the fourth stomach
The gallbladder
The small intestines
The rumen, the first and largest stomach
A handbreadth

phrases.english: If the abomasum was perforated, if the gallbladder was perforated,
if the small intestines were perforated;
the inner rumen that was perforated,
or where most of the outer rumen was torn.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
For a large animal, a handbreadth; and for a small one, most of it.
phrases.notes: He is talking about a tear in the outer rumen from the line before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of טרפות, moving on to the digestive organs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hole in the קבה, the מרה, or the דקין is a טרפה. Any hole in the inner כרס is a טרפה. The outer כרס is a טרפה only if most of it is torn, while רבי יהודה says a טפח in a large animal and most of it in a small one.

steps.title: The המסס and בית הכוסות pierced to the outside
steps.stepSummary: A hole in the המסס or the בית הכוסות makes the animal a טרפה only if it goes through to the outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the omasum or the reticulum got a hole that goes through to the outside, the animal is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds two more stomachs to the list, with the condition that the hole must go to the outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two stomachs sit next to each other. The words 'to the outside' teach that a hole opening from one of them into the other is not a טרפה. Only a hole that opens out into the body cavity counts.

keyTerms.meaning: The omasum, the third stomach
The reticulum, the second stomach
To the outside, meaning into the body cavity

steps.confusionAlert: Not every hole in these stomachs makes a טרפה. A hole that only connects the two stomachs to each other does not count.

phrases.english: The omasum and the reticulum that were perforated to the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of digestive organs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The המסס and בית הכוסות make an animal a טרפה only when pierced through to the outside.

steps.title: More טרפות and the general rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds three more cases: an animal that fell from a roof, one with most of its ribs broken, and one clawed by a wolf. רבי יהודה gives details about which predators count for which animals. The משנה ends with a rule: any animal that could not survive in this condition is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it fell from the roof, if most of its ribs were broken, or if a wolf clawed it, it is a טרפה. רבי יהודה says: a wolf's clawing counts for a small animal and a lion's clawing for a large animal; a hawk's clawing counts for a small bird and a large bird of prey's clawing for a large bird. This is the rule: any animal that could not live in this condition is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of טרפות and then sums everything up with one general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each new case is a serious injury: a fall, broken ribs, or a predator's claws. רבי יהודה matches the predator to the size of the victim, so a wolf counts against a sheep but not against a cow. The closing rule explains what all the cases share: the animal cannot survive.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal clawed by a predator
Ribs
Small animal (sheep, goat) / large animal (cattle)
Hawk
This is the general rule

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's key rule is: כל שאין כמוה חיה טרפה. An animal is a טרפה when its injury means it could not survive.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closing rule is exactly what the גמרא will now look for in the Torah.

phrases.english: If it fell from the roof,
or most of its ribs were broken,
or one clawed by a wolf.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: דְּרוּסַת הַזְּאֵב בַּדַּקָּה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: clawing by a wolf counts for a small animal,
and clawing by a lion for a large animal,
clawing by a hawk for a small bird,
and clawing by a large bird of prey for a large bird.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין כָּמוֹהָ חַיָּה – טְרֵפָה.
phrases.english: This is the rule: any animal that could not live in this condition is a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of טרפות and closes it with a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fall, most ribs broken, or a predator's clawing makes an animal a טרפה. In general, any animal that could not survive in its condition is a טרפה.

steps.title: Where does the Torah hint at טרפה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins. ריש לקיש asks where the Torah hints at טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: Where is there a hint to טרפה in the Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question from ריש לקיש looking for a Torah source for טרפה. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the word רמז (hint), which suggests he wants a hidden hint and not an open פסוק. As worded, though, the question sounds strange, and the גמרא will push back right away.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
A hint or allusion in the פסוק
From where do we know?

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Where is there a hint to tereifa in the Torah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah hint for the concept of טרפה.

steps.title: The Torah says טרפה openly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that no hint is needed, because the Torah openly forbids טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where?! The Torah says openly: "ובשר בשדה טרפה לא תאכלו", flesh torn in the field you shall not eat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש's question: why look for a hint when there is a clear פסוק?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on eating טרפה is written outright in שמות. So the question as worded makes no sense, and it must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Flesh torn in the field, the Torah's explicit term for טרפה

phrases.english: From where?!
"And flesh torn in the field you shall not eat"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the question in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's request for a hint to טרפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is an explicit פסוק, so no hint is needed.

steps.title: The real question: a טרפה cannot live
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the question. ריש לקיש was looking for a hint that a טרפה cannot live, an idea implied by the משנה's closing rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant: where is there a hint in the Torah that a טרפה cannot live? The last part of the משנה teaches: "This is the rule: any animal that could not live in this condition is a טרפה." That implies a טרפה cannot live. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own objection by explaining what ריש לקיש really meant. This sets up the real question that the next step answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on טרפה is explicit, but the idea that a טרפה is an animal that will not survive is not stated in that פסוק. That idea comes from the משנה's closing rule, so the גמרא now looks for its Torah source.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; it drops the first reading and offers a new one
The last part of the משנה
By implication
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Rather, a hint that a tereifa cannot live,
where is it in the Torah?
For the last part of the Mishna teaches:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַכְּלָל, כֹּל שֶׁאֵין כָּמוֹהָ חַיָּה – טְרֵפָה,
phrases.english: This is the rule: any animal that could not live in this condition is a tereifa,
which implies that a tereifa cannot live.
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, רֶמֶז לִטְרֵפָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ חַיָּה מִן הַתּוֹרָה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection in step 9 by rewording the question from step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah source showing that a טרפה cannot survive.

steps.title: Source: "וזאת החיה אשר תאכלו"
steps.stepSummary: The word חיה in the פסוק is read as "living": you may eat an animal that can live, but not one that cannot. This shows a טרפה cannot live.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "וזאת החיה אשר תאכלו", these are the living things you may eat. A living one, eat; one that is not living, do not eat. This implies that a טרפה cannot live.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק from ויקרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חיה can mean both "animal" and "living." Reading it as "living," the פסוק permits only animals that can survive. Since a טרפה is forbidden, it must be the kind that cannot survive.

keyTerms.meaning: These are the living things you may eat
Here it means "living" or "able to survive"

steps.confusionAlert: חיה usually means "animal" (often a wild animal), but this דרשה reads it as "living." The whole proof depends on that second meaning.

phrases.english: As it is written: "These are the living things which you may eat,"
a living one, eat;
one that is not living, do not eat.
This implies that a tereifa cannot live.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק "וזאת החיה אשר תאכלו" allows only an animal that can live, so a טרפה is one that cannot live.
steps.whatToRemember: The source that a טרפה cannot live: "וזאת החיה אשר תאכלו". Only a living, surviving animal may be eaten.

steps.title: What about the view that a טרפה can live?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the opinion that holds a טרפה can survive gets its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says a טרפה can live, where does he learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the opposite opinion and asks for its source. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not everyone agrees that a טרפה cannot survive. So the גמרא asks how that other opinion derives its view from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: A טרפה can live

phrases.english: And according to the one who says a tereifa can live,
from where does he learn it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר טְרֵפָה חַיָּה, מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first opinion's source to the opposing opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for the view that a טרפה can survive.

steps.title: Same פסוק, read the other way
steps.stepSummary: The other opinion learns from the word זאת ("these"): only these living animals may be eaten, not other living animals. So a טרפה is forbidden even though it is alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from "זאת החיה אשר תאכלו": "these" living things you may eat, but not other living things. This implies that a טרפה can live.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the opposing opinion uses the very same פסוק but stresses the word "these."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word זאת limits what may be eaten. Only these living animals are allowed, so there must be other animals that are living yet forbidden, and those are טרפות. That means a טרפה can be alive.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it from
Another living animal, meaning a טרפה

steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions use "זאת החיה אשר תאכלו". One stresses חיה (only living animals, so a טרפה cannot live). The other stresses זאת (only these living animals, so a טרפה can live and is still forbidden).

phrases.aramaic: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִ״זֹּאת הַחַיָּה אֲשֶׁר תֹּאכְלוּ״ –
phrases.english: He derives it from "These are the living things which you may eat":
"these living things" you may eat,
another living thing you may not eat.
phrases.notes: "Another living thing" means a טרפה, which is still alive but forbidden.

phrases.english: This implies that a tereifa can live.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִזֹּאת הַחַיָּה אֲשֶׁר תֹּאכְלוּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word זאת limits eating to "these" living animals and excludes other living ones, the טרפות, so a טרפה can live.

steps.title: What does the first opinion do with the word זאת?
steps.stepSummary: The opinion that a טרפה cannot live learned from חיה. The גמרא asks what that opinion does with the word זאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other opinion, what does it do with this word 'זאת'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to the first opinion, which says a טרפה cannot live. It asks what that opinion learns from the word זאת, since it did not use זאת for the טרפה rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 13 the opinion that a טרפה can live used זאת as its source. The opinion that a טרפה cannot live used חיה instead. Every word in the פסוק should teach something, so the גמרא asks what זאת teaches for this opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one; here, the other opinion
What does he do with it? What does he learn from this word?

phrases.english: And the other opinion, what does it do with this word 'these'?
phrases.notes: 'The other opinion' here means the one that holds a טרפה cannot live, from step 11.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving the source for the opinion that a טרפה can live, the גמרא checks how the first opinion uses that same word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the opinion that a טרפה cannot live learns from the word זאת.

steps.title: זאת teaches that God showed משה each animal
steps.stepSummary: The first opinion uses זאת for the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל: הקדוש ברוך הוא held up each kind of animal and showed it to משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'This is the animal that you may eat' teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא took hold of each and every kind, showed it to משה, and said: eat this one, and do not eat that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this opinion needs the word זאת for a different lesson. 'This' means God pointed to each animal and showed it to משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זאת means 'this,' as if pointing at something. The school of רבי ישמעאל reads it to mean that God actually showed משה each kind of animal. So זאת is already being used, and it is not left over for the טרפה rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for, meaning the word is already used for another lesson
It teaches
Kind or species of animal

phrases.aramaic: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
phrases.english: He needs it for that which the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught,
as the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'These are the living things which you may eat'
This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, took hold
of each and every kind
and showed it to Moses, and said to him:
This you may eat, and this you may not eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: זאת is used to teach that God showed משה each kind of animal and said which may and may not be eaten.

steps.title: The second opinion also needs זאת for that lesson
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the opinion that a טרפה can live should also need זאת for the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the other opinion also needs it for what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source from step 13. If זאת is needed to teach that God showed משה the animals, the opinion that a טרפה can live cannot also use זאת for the טרפה rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody argues with the lesson of the school of רבי ישמעאל, so both opinions must accept it. That means זאת is already taken for both opinions. So the source given in step 13 seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too

phrases.english: But the other opinion also needs it
phrases.notes: Now 'the other' means the opinion that a טרפה can live, the one from step 13.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ נָמֵי מִבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 15 against the source given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The source in step 13, that the opinion that a טרפה can live learns its rule from זאת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One word cannot be used for two lessons. If both opinions need זאת for the school of רבי ישמעאל's teaching, it is not free to teach the טרפה rule.

steps.title: The גמרא agrees and asks for a new source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the second opinion needs זאת for that lesson. So it asks again: where does that opinion learn that a טרפה can live?
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. Rather, where does he learn that a טרפה can live?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge and drops the source from step 13. It is setting up a new search for the source of the opinion that a טרפה can live.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אין הכי נמי' means the objection is correct. The question from step 12 is now open again. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so; the גמרא agrees with the objection
From where does he learn it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי, אֶלָּא טְרֵפָה חַיָּה מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the objection of step 16 and reopens the question of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession: the objection is accepted, and a new source will be given.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The opinion that a טרפה can live learned it from זאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: זאת is needed for another lesson, so this opinion needs a different source.

steps.title: The verse calls the forbidden animals 'living,' meaning the eighteen טרפות
steps.stepSummary: The second opinion learns its rule from another teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל. The verse speaks of 'the living thing that may not be eaten,' and that means the eighteen טרפות told to משה at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from another teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל: 'Between the living thing that may be eaten and the living thing that may not be eaten.' These are the eighteen טרפות that were told to משה at סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the new source. A verse calls the forbidden animals 'living things,' and the ברייתא says those forbidden animals are the טרפות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the forbidden 'living things' in the verse are the טרפות, then the Torah calls a טרפה 'living.' This shows that a טרפה can live. The ברייתא also says there are eighteen טרפות, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The eighteen kinds of טרפה
From סיני; taught to משה by tradition
The living thing that may not be eaten; the phrase this opinion uses to show a טרפה can live

steps.whatToRemember: The opinion that a טרפה can live does not learn it from זאת. It learns it from 'the living thing that may not be eaten,' which refers to the eighteen טרפות.

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the number eighteen טרפות, which the גמרא now goes on to question.

steps.title: Are there really only eighteen טרפות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: there seem to be more than eighteen טרפות. There are the cases remembered by the sign בסג״ר, and seven more rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And are there no more? But there are the cases of בסג״ר, and seven more rulings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the number eighteen in the ברייתא. It lists more טרפות that are known, so the count seems too low.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said there are exactly eighteen טרפות. But there are more cases, marked by the memory sign בסג״ר, plus seven more rulings. So how can the ברייתא say only eighteen? The answer comes on the next amud.
